paragraphs: An image classifier can learn relationships that work in its training environment but fail elsewhere because hidden factors influence those relationships. Causal approaches try to address this confounding, but their assumptions can be restrictive. Instrumental variables offer another route, although manually choosing suitable instruments for images risks introducing bias when the required conditions do not hold.

VIV-DG proposes learning visual instrumental variables automatically. Its starting observation is that certain non-causal visual attributes naturally meet the basic requirements for an instrument. The method extends instrumental-variable reasoning to visual representations and trains a learner that explicitly enforces the relevant conditions, rather than depending on a predefined choice of visual instrument.

The intended benefit is to reduce the influence of unobserved confounders while avoiding bias from invalid predefined instruments. Experiments across multiple benchmarks report stronger generalization. These findings support learning instruments as part of the image-classification system, with validity conditions playing a central role in how those representations are constructed.
neurips-2025-automatic-visual-instrument.tldr: VIV-DG automatically learns visual instrumental variables to reduce hidden confounding and improve image-classification generalization.

paragraphs: Designing a robot's body together with its controller can require substantial simulation, because many candidate bodies need control training. LOKI reduces that burden by grouping morphologically similar designs in a learned representation space and training shared control policies across each group. This lets related bodies reuse control knowledge during the design search.

The framework also changes how new bodies are explored. It replaces mutation with dynamic local search and combines broader exploration with local competition. These choices aim to avoid settling too early on a narrow family of designs. The authors report exploring approximately 780 times more designs using 78% fewer simulation steps and 40% less computation per design.

In the UNIMAL design space, training on flat-terrain locomotion produces varied bodies, including quadrupeds, crab-like designs, bipeds, and spinners. The resulting designs transfer better to tested agility, stability, and manipulation tasks, with twice the reward on bump and push-box-incline tasks. The results connect efficient policy reuse with both morphological diversity and adaptability.
neurips-2025-convergent-functions-diverg.tldr: LOKI reuses controllers across similar robot bodies to explore more designs efficiently and improve transfer to unseen tasks.

paragraphs: Knowledge-graph reasoning needs to distinguish plausible answers from incorrect entities. Combining nearby graph information with broader context can help, but existing approaches can make candidate scores too similar. This score over-smoothing weakens the distinction that the reasoning system ultimately needs to make.

DuetGraph addresses the problem with two separate processing pathways. One uses message passing for local information; the other uses attention for global information. Keeping these pathways distinct avoids the mutual interference associated with stacking their processing. A second component divides entities into higher- and lower-scoring subsets, then uses coarse-to-fine optimization to narrow the candidate space and increase separation between those subsets.

Across the evaluated datasets, the authors report state-of-the-art performance, with reasoning-quality improvements of up to 8.7% and a 1.8-fold acceleration in training efficiency. The contribution combines architectural separation with more focused optimization: both components are designed to preserve meaningful differences among candidate answers instead of letting those differences blur during reasoning.
neurips-2025-duetgraph-coarse-to-fine-kn.tldr: DuetGraph separates local and global graph processing and refines candidate scores to improve knowledge-graph reasoning.

paragraphs: RAW images retain information that can help object detectors in low light, before an image-processing pipeline converts the sensor output into sRGB. Using RAW images directly, however, brings storage and transmission costs and can require changes to downstream models. This paper explores how to retain useful RAW information within an existing imaging workflow.

The proposed CRM-IR scheme learns compact metadata from RAW images. A machine-vision-oriented refinement module uses that metadata to modify the corresponding sRGB images so they better support downstream recognition. The objective is to extract the most essential guidance from RAW data, allowing refinement without changing the detector architecture or the image signal processor.

Experiments with several object-detection networks show significant improvements under low-light conditions, with an additional bitrate below 0.001 bits per pixel. This result concerns the added metadata cost. The approach matters because it connects information available in RAW images to established sRGB-based detection pipelines through a very small accompanying representation.
neurips-2025-end-to-end-low-light-enhanc.tldr: CRM-IR uses tiny amounts of learned RAW metadata to refine sRGB images and improve low-light object detection.

paragraphs: Guidance helps image generators produce outputs that look better and match a requested class or text prompt. Widely used classifier-free guidance can trade diversity against quality and consistency. Some approaches separate these goals more effectively, but require an additional weaker model or more model evaluations at each sampling step.

Entropy Rectifying Guidance changes the attention mechanism of diffusion transformer architectures during inference. The paper presents this as a simple way to improve quality, diversity, and prompt consistency together. Its scope also includes unconditional generation, where there is no supplied text prompt or class condition to guide the image.

The authors report significant improvements in text-to-image, class-conditional, and unconditional generation. They also show that ERG can be combined with CADS and APG guidance methods for further improvements. These results identify inference-time attention changes as a useful way to influence generation and show that the method can complement other guidance strategies across the evaluated tasks.
neurips-2025-entropy-rectifying-guidance.tldr: ERG modifies attention during image generation to improve quality, diversity, and prompt consistency across conditional and unconditional tasks.

paragraphs: Conformal prediction represents uncertainty with sets of possible labels, targeting a specified frequency of containing the correct answer. Online methods update these sets as data distributions change. This paper examines what happens when the labels used for those updates are noisy, under the specific assumption of uniform label noise with a known noise rate.

The authors show that noise can create a persistent difference between the intended and actual miscoverage rates. Their correction is a robust pinball loss that provides an unbiased estimate of the clean-label loss without requiring ground-truth labels. This gives existing online conformal methods a corrected training signal under the studied noise model.

The theoretical result bounds both empirical and expected coverage errors at a rate proportional to one over the square root of the number of steps. Experiments show improved noise robustness across several online methods. The guarantee is tied to uniform noise and knowledge of its rate; within that setting, the correction addresses a systematic coverage error.
neurips-2025-exploring-the-noise-robustn.tldr: A corrected pinball loss restores online conformal coverage under uniform label noise with a known noise rate.

paragraphs: Selecting a small dataset or feature subset can involve two goals: retaining useful information and avoiding near-duplicate choices. This paper formalizes a problem that adds monotone submodular utility to a weighted diversity term, subject to a maximum subset size. Submodular utility captures diminishing returns, while diversity is measured by the distance between the closest selected pair.

GIST tackles this combined objective through a sequence of maximum independent set problems, using a bicriteria greedy procedure to approximate them. The algorithm guarantees an objective value at least half the optimum. This is a guarantee for the combined utility-and-diversity objective, rather than separate half-optimal guarantees for each component.

The paper also proves that approximation within a factor of 0.5584 is NP-hard, placing a computational barrier near its achieved guarantee. In a single-shot ImageNet data-sampling evaluation, GIST outperforms the compared state-of-the-art methods. Together, the results supply a practical selection algorithm, a worst-case performance guarantee, and evidence of usefulness for the tested sampling task.
neurips-2025-gist-greedy-independent-set.tldr: GIST selects useful, well-separated subsets with a one-half approximation guarantee and strong reported ImageNet sampling results.

paragraphs: Training an LLM agent is difficult when success is judged only after many interactions. A final reward says little about which earlier actions helped. GiGPO extends group-based reinforcement learning with two levels of comparison, giving the agent feedback about both complete trajectories and individual decisions.

At the episode level, it compares groups of full interaction sequences. At the step level, it finds environment states that recur across trajectories and groups the actions taken from those same states. These anchor-state groups provide more local relative-advantage estimates. The method builds these comparisons from existing rollouts, without a critic, auxiliary models, or extra rollout generation.

Evaluations use Qwen2.5 models on ALFWorld, WebShop, and search-augmented question answering. Reported gains over GRPO exceed 12% on ALFWorld and 9% on WebShop, with QA performance reaching 42.1% for the 3B model and 47.2% for 7B. The experiments maintain the same GPU memory overhead and rollout budget, with little or no additional time cost.
neurips-2025-group-in-group-policy-optim.tldr: GiGPO compares whole trajectories and actions from repeated states to improve LLM-agent credit assignment without extra rollouts.

paragraphs: Text embedding models map documents into vector spaces, but different models produce different coordinate systems. This paper introduces an unsupervised method for translating between those spaces without paired examples, access to the encoders, or predefined matches. The task is to relate representations using the available embedding vectors themselves.

The method translates embeddings through a universal latent representation associated with the semantic structure conjectured by the Platonic Representation Hypothesis. It reports high cosine similarity for translations between models that differ in architecture, parameter count, and training data. These findings support the usefulness of shared geometric structure for translation across the tested model pairs.

The paper also demonstrates a security implication. An adversary with access only to embedding vectors can extract sensitive document information sufficient for classification and attribute inference. Preserving semantic geometry across spaces therefore has consequences beyond interoperability: the experiments show that vectors can expose meaningful properties of their source documents even without access to the original encoder.
neurips-2025-harnessing-the-universal-ge.tldr: Unsupervised embedding translation reveals shared geometry across models and enables sensitive attribute inference from vectors alone.

paragraphs: Flow matching learns continuous dynamics that transform noise into data. Recent extensions incorporate higher-order information about these trajectories to improve expressiveness and sampling efficiency. This paper develops a unified theoretical treatment of ordinary flow matching and versions that use trajectory derivatives up to any chosen order K.

Its central construction turns an otherwise intractable higher-order loss into a conditional regression problem through marginalization. The resulting regression supplies exact gradients. The framework also identifies a consistency constraint, making explicit a requirement that accompanies the higher-order formulation. This connects a broad class of trajectory-based objectives to a tractable learning procedure.

For implementations using transformer networks, the authors establish sharp statistical rates for estimating nonparametric distributions. The rate has the form n raised to a negative exponent proportional to 1/d, with logarithmic factors suppressed. It matches minimax lower bounds up to those factors. The result gives theoretical support for the framework while retaining an explicit dependence on dimensionality in its sample-efficiency characterization.
neurips-2025-high-order-flow-matching-un.tldr: A unified higher-order flow-matching framework yields tractable regression objectives and statistical rates matching minimax bounds up to logarithmic factors.

paragraphs: Prefix caching reduces LLM inference costs by retaining computation that can be reused. When storage fills, the system must choose what to evict. A least-recently-used policy bases that choice on access history, but the paper identifies a substantial gap between this common policy and an optimal eviction algorithm.

Learned Prefix Caching adds a prediction about future use. It analyzes conversational content to estimate which conversations are likely to continue, then combines that information with last-access timestamps. The eviction decision therefore reflects both when a conversation was last used and what its content suggests about whether it will be used again.

Across three real-world datasets, LPC reduces required cache capacity by 18–47% at equivalent hit ratios. In an emulated environment, it also improves LLM prefilling throughput by 11%. The capacity result means comparable cache reuse with less storage, while the throughput finding shows a measured processing benefit in the emulation. Together, they support content-aware prediction as a useful addition to recency-based cache management.
neurips-2025-learned-prefix-caching-for-.tldr: LPC predicts conversation continuation to improve prefix-cache eviction, reducing cache needs and increasing prefilling throughput in reported evaluations.

paragraphs: Weather data assimilation depends on estimating how forecasts are wrong before incorporating observations. Operational hybrid methods combine long-term error statistics with uncertainty estimated from an ensemble for the current atmospheric flow. Their Gaussian assumptions and handcrafted covariance structures can restrict how well they represent complex atmospheric errors.

LoRA-EnVar first trains a variational autoencoder on historical data to learn a climatological distribution of forecast errors. It then uses low-rank adaptation modules to adjust that distribution using flow-dependent ensemble perturbations. This supports online updates while avoiding catastrophic forgetting, allowing the learned error model to respond to current conditions without fully retraining its parameters.

Tests use the FengWu forecast model with simulated observations from ERA5 reanalysis in high-resolution assimilation settings. LoRA-EnVar improves assimilation accuracy over models with static error distributions and matches or exceeds full fine-tuning while using three orders of magnitude fewer trainable parameters. These findings support parameter-efficient adaptation as a promising route toward scalable assimilation with non-Gaussian error models.
neurips-2025-lora-envar-parameter-effici.tldr: LoRA-EnVar efficiently adapts learned weather-forecast error distributions to current conditions, improving assimilation with far fewer trainable parameters.

paragraphs: LLM serving systems face changing demand while trying to meet service-level objectives. One option is to run a model in FP16 normally and switch to FP8 during demand surges, gaining throughput with a slight quality reduction. Storing separate copies for both modes, however, adds a substantial memory burden.

NestedFP supports both precisions by overlaying FP8 parameters onto FP16 parameters within the memory footprint of the FP16 model. A compact representation makes this sharing possible. A specialized matrix-multiplication kernel is designed to operate efficiently with that representation, connecting the storage format to the computation used during inference.

The paper reports minimal degradation in model quality and inference throughput across both modes. Its contribution is a memory-efficient platform for choosing precision dynamically according to serving requirements. By making two precision modes available within one FP16-sized parameter footprint, NestedFP addresses the storage cost that otherwise accompanies switching between them as demand changes.
neurips-2025-nestedfp-high-performance-m.tldr: NestedFP shares one FP16-sized parameter footprint between FP16 and FP8 modes to support memory-efficient, demand-aware LLM serving.

paragraphs: Recovering an animatable human avatar from one or a few images is harder when accurate pose information is unavailable. Many leading reconstruction methods use camera and human poses supplied at test time. The paper shows that reconstruction quality can deteriorate substantially when those pose estimates are noisy.

NoPo-Avatar reconstructs the avatar from images alone, requiring no pose inputs. Removing human-pose estimates from the test-time input also removes their noise as a source of reconstruction error. This changes the information needed to use the method, making it applicable to settings where images are available but reliable pose annotations are not.

Experiments on THuman2.0, XHuman, and HuGe100K compare practical settings without ground-truth poses with laboratory settings where those poses are available. NoPo-Avatar outperforms existing baselines in the practical setting and achieves comparable results in the laboratory setting. The findings show the value of reducing dependence on privileged inputs while retaining competitive reconstruction quality when evaluated against pose-assisted methods.
neurips-2025-nopo-avatar-generalizable-a.tldr: NoPo-Avatar reconstructs animatable human avatars from sparse images without pose inputs, improving results when ground-truth poses are unavailable.

paragraphs: Low-rank adaptation fine-tunes foundation models through a limited set of trainable directions. How those directions are initialized affects adaptation. Existing approaches based on weight or gradient decompositions do not provably maximize the expected gradient signal. EVA instead selects directions that capture the most variation in the model's activations.

The method incrementally applies singular value decomposition to minibatches of activation vectors. Once the directions converge, it uses the right-singular vectors for initialization. The paper proves that this choice maximizes the expected gradient signal. EVA also redistributes ranks under a given budget, prioritizing directions with greater activation variance and reducing the number of trainable parameters.

Evaluations span language generation and understanding, image classification, and reinforcement learning. EVA converges faster than competing initialization methods and achieves the highest average score across the evaluated tasks in each domain. Its reported accuracy and efficiency tradeoffs improve on existing LoRA initialization schemes, connecting an activation-based initialization rule to both faster adaptation and more effective parameter allocation.
neurips-2025-parameter-efficient-fine-tu.tldr: EVA initializes and allocates LoRA directions using activation variance, improving fine-tuning speed, accuracy, and parameter efficiency.

paragraphs: Antibody design involves choosing both a molecular sequence and its structure, while balancing interaction preferences at an antigen's binding site. This paper develops a three-stage framework that first learns from millions of antibody sequences. Those learned representations then guide a diffusion model that jointly optimizes antibody sequences and structures.

The final stage aligns generation toward lower repulsion and greater attraction at the binding site. Because energy objectives can conflict, the authors extend Antibody Direct Preference Optimization to pursue Pareto-optimal tradeoffs across multiple objectives. An iterative learning procedure with temperature scaling allows the model to benefit from diverse online datasets without requiring additional data.

Experiments report stable, efficient generation and a better Pareto front than top samples from baselines and earlier alignment methods. A better front represents improved tradeoffs among the energy objectives, rather than a single score that hides their tensions. The paper also reports stronger generation of nature-like antibodies with high binding affinity, supporting multi-objective alignment for sequence-and-structure co-design.
neurips-2025-pareto-optimal-energy-align.tldr: A three-stage antibody-design framework aligns joint sequence-and-structure generation toward better tradeoffs among competing binding-energy objectives.

paragraphs: In-context learning can involve recognizing a previously learned task or learning how to perform a task from the examples currently provided. This paper asks how those two abilities develop during pretraining. The distinction matters because successful use of a prompt can reflect different mixtures of stored task knowledge and learning from context.

To make the learning dynamics analytically accessible, the authors study random linear regression with a simple transformer based on linear attention. They define separate measures of task recognition and task learning in the model's parameters. This setup allows them to track the two capabilities independently as pretraining proceeds.

Early in training, both abilities develop together. Later, the model gradually loses its ability to recall previously learned tasks and relies more on the supplied context. The authors call these effects prior forgetting and in-context overfitting. The result characterizes a shift within the studied regression-and-transformer setting, showing that continued pretraining need not preserve the balance between these two forms of in-context learning.
neurips-2025-prior-forgetting-and-in-con.tldr: In a simplified transformer setting, later pretraining weakens task recognition while increasing reliance on the current context.

paragraphs: Most deep networks build complex functions by alternating linear transformations with nonlinear activation functions. QuadEnhancer explores adding quadratic transformations to increase the model's nonlinearity further. The goal is to improve existing architectures while keeping the extra parameters and forward-pass computation small enough to make the enhancement practical.

The proposed module combines matrix decomposition, weight sharing, and sparsification to control its cost. These techniques keep the quadratic component lightweight instead of allowing the extra transformation to create a large parameter or computation burden. The paper reports that the resulting increase in both parameters and forward computation is minimal and negligible.

The authors evaluate the enhancer on text classification, image classification, and large-language-model fine-tuning, reporting significant performance gains in all three task categories. The findings suggest that explicitly adding quadratic transformations can improve the tested architectures without a substantial increase in their stated forward-computation cost. The contribution is therefore both a richer transformation and an economical way to incorporate it.
neurips-2025-quadenhancer-leveraging-qua.tldr: QuadEnhancer adds lightweight quadratic transformations to neural networks, improving tested tasks with negligible reported parameter and forward-computation overhead.

paragraphs: Retrieval-augmented generation can be manipulated through malicious documents in its retrieval corpus. ReliabilityRAG uses information about document reliability, such as search ranking, to help defend against this corruption. Its motivating setting is web search, where retrieval already supplies signals that can inform which documents deserve more weight.

The first method constructs a graph whose edges represent contradictions between documents. A reliability-prioritized maximum independent set procedure seeks a mutually consistent collection, filtering malicious material through a consistent-majority perspective. Its robustness guarantees apply to bounded adversarial corruption under stated natural assumptions. Because exact maximum independent set computation is costly, a second weighted sampling-and-aggregation method scales to larger retrieval sets while retaining some guarantees.

Experiments report stronger attack robustness than prior methods while maintaining high accuracy on benign inputs. ReliabilityRAG also performs well on long-form generation, where earlier robustness-focused approaches struggled. The framework connects reliability signals and agreement among sources, with separate approaches addressing strong combinatorial filtering and scalable processing.
neurips-2025-reliabilityrag-effective-an.tldr: ReliabilityRAG combines document reliability and consistency to defend retrieval-augmented generation, with conditional robustness guarantees and scalable aggregation.

paragraphs: A facial animation rig needs controlled deformations that turn a neutral mesh into expressions. RigAnyFace predicts these deformations for standard Facial Action Coding System poses, creating a blendshape rig. It handles varied mesh topologies, including faces with disconnected parts such as separate eyeballs.

Its surface-learning network is designed to work independently of a particular triangulation, condition predictions on facial-action parameters, and process disconnected components efficiently. Training uses a professionally rigged subset of a curated mesh dataset for accurate 3D supervision. Because manual rigging is costly, that labeled subset alone limits the diversity available for learning.

The authors add a 2D supervision strategy that can use neutral meshes without existing rigs. This expands the training data and improves generalization. Experiments on artist-created assets and in-the-wild samples report better accuracy and generalizability than previous methods. The contribution combines broader mesh compatibility with a way to learn from unlabeled assets, while supporting more detailed animation through disconnected components.
neurips-2025-riganyface-scaling-neural-f.tldr: RigAnyFace uses unlabeled meshes and 2D supervision to scale facial auto-rigging across diverse topologies and disconnected components.

paragraphs: Safety alignment for multimodal assistants must address harmful behavior while preserving useful capabilities. A single preference label can entangle these goals, making safety constraints difficult to study separately. Safe RLHF-V introduces data and optimization tools that distinguish helpfulness preferences from safety preferences.

Its BeaverTails-V dataset supplies dual preference annotations and safety labels at minor, moderate, and severe levels. Beaver-Guard-V provides a multilevel guardrail against unsafe queries and adversarial attacks. Across five rounds of filtering and regeneration, applying this guard improves the precursor model's overall safety by an average of 40.9%.

The framework also studies multimodal alignment through constrained optimization using the separate preference signals. Reported experiments improve safety by 34.2% and helpfulness by 34.3%. These alignment results are distinct from the guardrail's filtering-and-regeneration result. Together, they show how explicit safety information can support both protective filtering and model optimization, with improvements in both helpfulness and safety in the evaluated setting.
neurips-2025-safe-rlhf-v-safe-reinforcem.tldr: Safe RLHF-V separates helpfulness and safety feedback to support multimodal guardrails and constrained alignment that improves both measured goals.

paragraphs: Protein language models can generate sequences for design tasks, but the effects of model size and training-data composition need systematic study. This paper introduces ProGen3, a family of sparse generative models, and develops compute-optimal scaling laws to guide expansion to a 46-billion-parameter model.

Training uses 1.5 trillion amino-acid tokens sampled from an optimized distribution over PPA v1, a curated collection of 3.4 billion full-length proteins. The study examines model scale through wet-lab evaluation of generated sequences. Larger models produce viable proteins across a substantially wider range of protein families in these experiments.

The authors also investigate alignment with laboratory data. Both computational and experimental results show that larger models respond more effectively to this alignment, improving protein fitness prediction and sequence generation. The findings connect scale with broader viable generation and better use of laboratory feedback. They support large models trained on carefully curated data as foundations for protein design across a wider diversity of families.
neurips-2025-scaling-unlocks-broader-gen.tldr: ProGen3 studies show that larger protein language models generate viable proteins across more families and benefit more from laboratory-data alignment.

paragraphs: Real time-series data often arrive at different rates, combine several modalities, and contain missing observations. Benchmarks built around clean, regularly sampled data can miss these difficulties. Time-IMM is designed to represent irregularity through its causes, covering nine types grouped into trigger-based, constraint-based, and artifact-based mechanisms.

The accompanying IMM-TSF library provides forecasting benchmarks that integrate modalities asynchronously. It includes timestamp-to-text fusion and multimodality fusion modules, with options for recency-aware averaging and attention-based integration. These components let the benchmark account for both the different information sources and their timing, rather than requiring every observation to share a regular schedule.

The reported experiments find substantial forecasting gains from explicitly modeling multimodality in irregular data. This supports treating the combination of information sources as part of the forecasting problem itself. The publicly available dataset and library provide a shared basis for evaluating models under the kinds of asynchronous sampling and missingness that motivate the work.
neurips-2025-time-imm-a-dataset-and-benc.tldr: Time-IMM and IMM-TSF provide data and forecasting tools for irregular multimodal time series, showing gains from explicitly combining modalities.

paragraphs: TTS-VAR improves visual autoregressive generation by treating inference as a search over possible generation paths. These models build images from coarse to fine scales, so the framework uses different search strategies at different stages. Its motivation is to improve outputs through test-time computation rather than additional model scaling during training.

At coarse scales, partial outputs are difficult to judge, even though they already contain useful structural information. TTS-VAR clusters semantic features to preserve structurally diverse candidates for later selection. At finer scales, it resamples candidates using potential scores that incorporate the generation history across scales. An adaptive schedule decreases batch size as generation proceeds to balance exploration and computation.

On Infinity2B, the method raises GenEval from 0.69 to 0.75, a reported 8.7% improvement. The findings indicate that early structural choices influence final quality and that resampling effectiveness varies by scale. This supports allocating search effort according to the stage of image formation instead of treating all generation steps alike.
neurips-2025-tts-var-a-test-time-scaling.tldr: TTS-VAR searches diverse coarse structures and resamples promising fine-scale candidates to improve visual autoregressive generation at inference time.

paragraphs: Long generated videos can gradually lose consistency as errors in object structure and motion accumulate. WorldWeaver addresses this drift by jointly modeling color frames and perceptual conditions over long sequences. Its premise is that RGB information alone does not provide the strongest basis for maintaining coherent structure through time.

The framework predicts perceptual conditions and color from a shared representation to improve temporal consistency and motion dynamics. It also builds a memory bank using depth cues, which the authors observe to resist drift better than RGB. A segmented noise schedule for training prediction groups further reduces drift and computational cost.

Experiments with both diffusion and rectified-flow models report reduced temporal drift and higher video fidelity. The contribution combines richer predicted information, depth-based contextual memory, and a training schedule designed for extended generation. These results support using perceptual structure throughout the generation process to help preserve context and motion over longer videos.
neurips-2025-worldweaver-generating-long.tldr: WorldWeaver combines perceptual prediction, depth-based memory, and segmented noise scheduling to reduce drift in long video generation.
